title: Wage effects of global value chains participation and position: an industry-level analysis
publisher: Journal of International Trade & Economic Development 31(7), 1086–1107
summary: The paper studies how participation and position in global value chains (GVCs) affect wages, comparing developed and developing countries and different labour market regulations.
keyFindings: In developed countries, GVC participation and upstream specialisation are both associated with higher wages.
In developing countries, participation is linked to higher wages, but upstream specialisation puts downward pressure on them.
In developing countries, participation mainly benefits higher earners; the positive wage effect appears only under stringent labour market regulation.
methods: Industry-level analysis across developed and developing countries (earlier version: UNU-MERIT Working Paper 2021-042).
